approval.cost: Not stated (Marketplace listing cost likewise not stated on the submission page read; paid apps are supported via Stripe, which is the developer charging customers, not a Zendesk listing fee)
approval.trigger: For multi-customer distribution, yes: you cannot self-create a global OAuth client. You request one via the Zendesk Marketplace portal (apps.zendesk.com > Global OAuth > Request new OAuth, specifying the scopes your app requires), from a sponsored developer account whose subdomain includes the prefix 'd3v-' ('Submissions from non-d3v- accounts aren't accepted'). 'You'll receive an email and a ticket reference with updates on your submission.' 'If the request is approved, Zendesk converts your local OAuth client to a global OAuth client', and Zendesk may configure allowed scopes on it: 'If your app requests a scope that is not included in the client's allowed scopes, the authorization request fails with a 400 Bad Request response and an invalid_scope error, no token is issued.' Until approval, the functional cap is one Zendesk account (the client works only on its own instance). Marketplace LISTING is a separate submission through the Marketplace developer portal, with a stated turnaround of '1-3 weeks for new app submissions and 1-2 week for updates to existing apps'; approved listings are published by 10am PST the next day.
approval.wait: Global OAuth approval: not stated. Marketplace listing: 1-3 weeks for new submissions, 1-2 weeks for updates (stated)

blockers.detail: 'Make sure you note down the secret and the identifier before making your request. You will lose access to the client administration page after the local client is converted to a global client.' After conversion the client 'can only be edited by our Marketplace Operations Team'; changes, including allowed-scope changes, require contacting Zendesk Support (mention 'global oauth' / 'global oauth allowed scopes', include the client_id).
blockers.howToClear: Freeze the client's configuration and scope set before requesting conversion, and vault the identifier and secret first.
blockers.title: The conversion is a one-way door

blockers.detail: The Unique Identifier must be prefixed with 'zdg-', must be representative of your product ('zdg-zendesk' is acceptable but 'zdg-global_client1' is not), and must be 'the exact value intended for production'. 'Complete all fields. Even if a field is labeled optional, it is required for global clients.' Use a separate client per app. A sloppy local client cannot be quietly fixed later because conversion removes your edit access.
blockers.howToClear: Create the local client deliberately as the future global client from day one.
blockers.title: Global-request naming and field traps

blockers.detail: 'Zendesk maintains separate logins for each Zendesk account or subdomain. When a customer signs in, they're signing into a specific Zendesk subdomain which carries over to OAuth.' Tokens are tied to the authorizing user and that instance and 'inherit that user's permissions' (role changes automatically change token access). Client-credentials tokens are tied to the client's creator, so if that user is downgraded, the integration can break.
blockers.howToClear: Build subdomain-aware token storage and treat user role changes as a live variable, not an edge case.
blockers.title: Per-instance architecture

flavor.recommended: A global OAuth client (converted from your local client by Zendesk) using the authorization code flow with a confidential client
flavor.why: The object is an OAuth client in two kinds: local ('OAuth clients are scoped to one Zendesk instance') and global (works across multiple Zendesk accounts). For multi-customer distribution the global client is effectively mandatory: 'If you plan on making an app, integration, or bot available to multiple Zendesk customers, you must use global OAuth access tokens. You may not use regular API tokens or OAuth tokens because the Zendesk Developer Terms prohibits Zendesk customers from sharing their API credentials with you.' Client kinds: public (cannot securely store a secret; PKCE required) or confidential (can hold a secret server-side). Note: global clients cover Zendesk Support and Chat (Agent Workspace) only; Zendesk Sell needs a separate Multi-User Application registration.

name: Zendesk
nuances: Authorization codes are valid for only 120 seconds and single-use ('exchange it as soon as possible').

Token lifetime rules are unusually configurable: expires_in must be >= 300 seconds (5 minutes) and <= 172,800 seconds (2 days), or less than refresh_token_expires_in. Defaults: null (no expiry) for clients created before April 30, 2026; 1,800 seconds (30 minutes) for clients created on or after that date. refresh_token_expires_in must be >= 604,800 seconds (7 days) and <= 7,776,000 seconds (90 days), defaulting to 2,592,000 (30 days).

Legacy-client trap: 'For OAuth clients created before April 30, 2026, there is no default access token expiration. If you are using a legacy client and want to use refresh tokens, you must explicitly pass expires_in when creating the token. If you omit it, the access token will not expire, and a refresh token will not be generated.' Existing tokens also cannot be converted into ones with refresh tokens.

Refresh tokens are single-use and rotating: 'After you exchange a refresh token for a new access token, you must store and use the new refresh token returned in the response'; previous access and refresh tokens are invalidated.

Scope error asymmetry: a scope outside the client's allowed scopes fails fast (400 / invalid_scope, no token), but an UNRECOGNIZED scope string 'still creates an access token. However, any API request made with that token will return a 403 Forbidden error.'

Scope model: broad read ('Read all data') and write, granular resource:action scopes (tickets:read, users:write), plus impersonate (admins acting on behalf of end users via the X-On-Behalf-Of header). Effective access is the intersection of token scope and the authorizing user's permissions. The password grant type 'has been deprecated and is highly discouraged'. Access tokens can be up to 184 characters; the full token value is only returned at creation.
prerequisites: A Zendesk account where you are an admin (or hold the Manage APIs permission)
For the global request: a sponsored developer account whose subdomain includes the 'd3v-' prefix
A local client created deliberately as the future global client (zdg- prefixed identifier, all fields complete)

steps.detail: Admin Center > Apps and integrations > APIs > OAuth clients (or POST /api/v2/oauth/clients.json). Set Client name, Unique identifier (prefix it 'zdg-' and make it the exact production value if it will go global), Redirect URLs, Client kind (Confidential for server apps), and optional Allowed scopes. Complete ALL fields, even ones labeled optional. Securely save the Identifier and Secret (the secret is returned in full only at creation).

steps.detail: Redirect the user to {subdomain}.zendesk.com/oauth/authorizations/new?response_type=code&client_id=...&redirect_uri=...&scope=...&state=... (redirect_uri must exactly match the configured value). The user signs in to THEIR subdomain and approves; denial returns error=access_denied. Exchange the code (valid only 120 seconds, single-use) at POST {subdomain}.zendesk.com/oauth/tokens with grant_type=authorization_code, code, client_id, client_secret (or PKCE code_verifier), redirect_uri, and optional scope, expires_in, refresh_token_expires_in. Call the API with Authorization: Bearer against {subdomain}.zendesk.com/api/v2/...

steps.detail: When the app is finished: note down the secret and identifier first (you lose the admin page after conversion). Sign in to the Zendesk Marketplace portal (apps.zendesk.com) > Global OAuth > Request new OAuth, from a sponsored account whose subdomain includes 'd3v-', and complete the form specifying your required scopes. Zendesk emails you a ticket reference; if approved, Zendesk converts your local client to a global client and may configure its allowed scopes.

tagline: Two-tier OAuth: a local client works instantly but only inside one Zendesk instance, while selling to many customers requires a global client that Zendesk must approve and convert for you, after which Zendesk owns all edits to it. Marketplace listing, if you want it, adds a stated 1 to 3 week review.
